summary: Procurement + legal intake focused on MSA/DPA redlines, pricing objections around pilot vs reserved capacity, KMS integration questions, and next steps to run a short PoC. High-level alignment on technical feasibility; legal needs liability cap and clearer audit language; security wants KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence.
topics: Pricing model: pilot vs reserved commits
Next steps: redlines, pricing worksheet, PoC telemetry
transcript: [00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about an hour. Quick roll call?
[00:14] Marta (Talos Proc): Marta here — procurement. We just want to make sure commercial path is clear before we loop in finance.
[00:22] Ethan (Talos Legal): Ethan on the call for legal, I'll be routing MSA/DPA redlines.
[00:27] Samira (Talos Sec): Samira, security, hi. We'll be focused on KMS, audit, SOC2 and any fedramp implications.
[00:33] Benji (Talos Eng): Benji — platform eng, I can speak to traffic patterns and integration constraints.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya from the solutions team, I'll cover the pilot sizing and the KMS handoff. Aidan from CSM is also on but quiet for notes.
[01:05] Jordan: Great. Agenda — clarify the outstanding commercial asks, go through MSA/DPA points Ethan flagged, KMS and SSO notes, then pricing and PoC mechanics. Sound good?
[01:22] Marta: Yes. Our procurement review has a couple of sticking points on pricing — primarily burst costs and termination liability. We need clearer billing paths.
[01:34] Priya: Understood — for the pilot we typically recommend a usage-based pass-through with a short reserved window option if you expect steady load. We can put numbers in a worksheet.

[01:48] Benji: From eng perspective — our traffic is spiky; normal weekdays 200-300 qps with burst to 1k qps for peaks. We need to understand throttling and predictable overage rates. There's also KV cache concerns.

[02:09] Priya: KV cache — we can set prefix caching and recommended batching to reduce token usage. We'll include burst capacity guidance and what that looks like on Dedicated vs Hosted. Sometimes the docs say 'Redwood Privet' in our internal notes — ignore that typo.
[02:30] Ethan: On MSA, big asks: liability cap, data processing audit rights, and retention terms in the DPA. Also, indemnity around models producing PII is a concern.
[02:45] Jordan: For liability cap we typically align to a multiple of fees; for enterprise we can discuss a higher cap. What's your target?
[02:58] Ethan: Talos' standard is 3x ARR or $5M floor, whichever is lower. We know vendors push back, so want to surface it now.
[03:08] Jordan: Noted. We'll take that back. On DPA retention — can you clarify retention windows and deletion controls you require?

[03:18] Samira: We need the ability to specify retention per-tenant, hard-delete on request, and proof of deletion logs. Also we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) in an HSM — bring-your-own-key (BYOK) or KMS is a must.

[03:36] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for private deployments; Hosted can integrate with cloud KMS in many regions. We'll document the exact APIs and the key rotation model.
[03:50] Benji: For onboarding we also need an access matrix and RBAC mapping; SSO via SAML is required. Does Redwood support SCIM for provisioning?
[03:59] Aidan (Redwood CSM): We do support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in enterprise plans. We'll include the SCIM endpoints and sample mapping.

[04:15] Marta: Pricing — our procurement wants a clear committed path so finance can forecast. The pilot needs to be inexpensive but with optional escalation to committed monthly reserveds. How do you usually structure that?

[04:29] Priya: We offer a short pilot with a capped monthly spend and a follow-up reserved commit with a discount tier. For bursts we have a burst pool add-on and also can do predictable latency SLOs if you go Dedicated. I'll prepare a worksheet showing token burn under 3 sample traffic profiles.

[04:48] Ethan: On legal timing, we need a tracked redline. Also, what's your stance on audit rights? Customers often want on-demand audit or third-party audit reports. SOC2 + ISO is fine, FedRAMP is heavier.

[05:02] Jordan: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports. For FedRAMP we have a path but it's longer; we can discuss a tailored addendum for audit access — typical approach is annual third-party attestation plus limited audit rights with NDAs.
[05:20] Samira: We'll need to see the SOC2 report and a list of subprocessors. Also the encryption-in-transit and at-rest details — what ciphers, TLS versions, and key lifecycle?

[05:33] Priya: We'll add a security appendix — TLS 1.2/1.3, AES-256 at rest, and details on KMS integrations. Note: sometimes names are munged in auto transcripts — 'KV cache' becomes 'K V cash', so flag any oddities in the docs.
[05:50] Benji: On SLA — we require a 99.95% uptime SLO for the production path. If that's not in standard hosted, is Dedicated required?
[06:05] Jordan: 99.95% is generally offered at Dedicated tier with SLA-backed credits. Hosted is usually 99.9% for standard. We can outline SLA tiers and associated credits.
[06:18] Marta: Procurement will push back on unlimited data egress fees; we need transparent egress and network cost breakdowns. Also clarify who pays for KMS HSM costs.
[06:33] Priya: We'll include an egress and KMS cost example. In many cases KMS HSM is billed pass-through or included in enterprise pricing; we'll call that out.
[06:45] Ethan: Also, data residency: Talos wants EU data stored in EU region only. Are there region restrictions?
[06:55] Priya: We support region pinning for Private and Dedicated; Hosted can pin to region-aware clusters in select clouds — we'll list available regions and residency guarantees.
[07:08] Samira: About keys, can we have BYOK with HSM so keys never leave our control?
[07:14] Priya: Yes for Private/Dedicated we support BYOK and HSM integrations. Hosted with BYOK depends on cloud provider — we'll capture specifics.
[07:25] Benji: For the PoC telemetry, we need to know what metrics Redwood will expose — per-route latency, token counts, cache hit rates, error traces.
[07:36] Aidan: We'll expose token-level cost, latency per model, cache hit rate, and request traces in the Console. We'll share a sample telemetry export.
[07:48] Marta: If procurement approves, timeline is two weeks for contracting and three weeks to pilot. We need to align on decision gates.
[07:58] Jordan: OK. Proposed timeline: Jordan sends MSA/DPA redlines within 5 business days; tech PoC starts after sign-of-order and takes 2-3 weeks. Any blockers to that?
[08:09] Ethan: Legal wants to review redlines first; we'll need 3 business days to revert. Indemnity will be a negotiation point. Also adding audit clause might take longer.
[08:22] Jordan: Understood. We'll flag the indemnity and audit items as heads-up in our redline. For pricing objections, Priya will produce concrete numbers for pilot vs reserved commit.

[08:32] Priya: I'll run three profiles (light, medium, heavy) showing per-token and reserved savings and the expected billing under your burst pattern. I'll include a Dedicated vs Hosted delta so you can see SLO tradeoffs.
[08:45] Benji: One quick technical question — how is model fallback handled if a region is constrained? We need deterministic behavior to avoid flaky responses.

[08:57] Priya: We have routing policies — failover to a compatible model or a different region based on your policy; we can pin models to prevent silent fallback. We'll share the routing policy doc. Sometimes the transcript shows 'routeing' spelled weird.
[09:12] Samira: Also confirm logs: per-tenant audit logs with immutable timestamps and optional SIEM integration?
[09:20] Aidan: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3 with retention controls.
